notes.title: Introduction to Units
notes.content: Physical quantities are classified into fundamental and derived quantities. The SI system is the standard used globally. Fundamental units include Meter (m), Kilogram (kg), Second (s), Ampere (A), Kelvin (K), Mole (mol), and Candela (cd).

notes.title: Dimensional Analysis Formulas
notes.content:
• Dimension of Force = [MLT^-2]
  • Dimension of Energy = [ML^2T^-2]
  • Dimension of Power = [ML^2T^-3]
  • Dimension of Pressure = [ML^-1T^-2]

notes.title: The Mole Concept
notes.content: One mole contains 6.022 x 10^23 particles. This number is known as Avogadros constant. Molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance in grams.

notes.title: Introduction to C
notes.content: C is a general-purpose, procedural computer programming language supporting structured programming, lexical variable scope, and recursion, with a static type system. It was developed by Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs.

notes.title: Control Structures
notes.content:
Control structures in C include:
  • if-else: Conditional execution
  • switch: Multi-way branching
  • loops: for, while, do-while

notes.title: HTML Structure
notes.content: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser. Key tags include <html>, <head>, <body>, <div>, <span>.

notes.title: SQL Commands
notes.content:
SQL commands are grouped into:
  • DDL: CREATE, ALTER, DROP
  • DML: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
  • DCL: GRANT, REVOKE

notes.title: Scalars and Vectors
notes.content:
Scalars have magnitude only (e.g., mass, temperature). Vectors have magnitude and direction (e.g., displacement, velocity, force). A vector is represented graphically by an arrow; its length denotes magnitude and its orientation denotes direction.

Vector addition follows the parallelogram or triangle law. Resultant R of A and B: R = A + B. Subtraction uses A − B = A + (−B).

Dot product: A · B = |A||B|cosθ. Cross product: A × B = |A||B|sinθ n̂.

notes.title: Vector Identities
notes.content:
• Unit vector: â = A/|A|
  • Magnitude of cross product: |A × B| = |A||B|sinθ
  • Scalar projection: compB(A) = (A · B)/|B|
  • Vector projection: projB(A) = ((A · B)/|B|^2) B

notes.title: Kinematics Basics
notes.content:
Kinematics describes motion without considering causes. Key quantities: displacement, velocity, and acceleration.

For uniform acceleration in one dimension, motion is described by the equations of motion. Projectile motion decomposes into independent horizontal and vertical components.

notes.title: Equations of Motion
notes.content:
• v = u + at
  • s = ut + ½at^2
  • v^2 = u^2 + 2as
  • Projectile time of flight: T = (2u sinθ)/g
  • Range: R = (u^2 sin2θ)/g

notes.title: Quantum Numbers
notes.content:
Each electron in an atom is described by four quantum numbers: n (principal), l (azimuthal), ml (magnetic), and ms (spin). They define energy level, subshell shape, orientation, and spin.

Pauli exclusion states no two electrons can have the same set of four quantum numbers. Hund’s rule favors maximum multiplicity in degenerate orbitals.

notes.title: Arithmetic Progression
notes.content:
An AP has a constant difference d between consecutive terms. If a is the first term, the n-th term is Tn = a + (n−1)d.

Sum of first n terms: Sn = n/2[2a + (n−1)d].

notes.title: Logic Gates Overview
notes.content: Basic gates: AND, OR, NOT; derived gates: NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR. Truth tables define gate behavior. Boolean algebra simplifies logical expressions for digital circuit design.

notes.title: Cell Organelles
notes.content: Key organelles: nucleus (genetic control), mitochondria (ATP production), ribosomes (protein synthesis), ER and Golgi (processing and transport), lysosomes (digestion), chloroplasts in plants (photosynthesis).

notes.title: SI Base Units Overview
notes.content:
The International System of Units (SI) defines seven base units: second (time), metre (length), kilogram (mass), ampere (electric current), kelvin (thermodynamic temperature), mole (amount of substance), and candela (luminous intensity). All other units are derived from these.

Source: Wikipedia — SI base unit

notes.title: Stoichiometry Basics
notes.content:
Stoichiometry studies quantitative relationships between reactants and products using balanced chemical equations and the conservation of mass. It relates moles, molar ratios, and masses to predict product amounts and required reactant quantities.

Source: Wikipedia — Stoichiometry

notes.title: Wave Optics — Detailed Notes
notes.content:
Interference

The superposition of two coherent light waves resulting in regions of maximum and minimum intensity.

  • Young’s Double Slit Experiment (YDSE): Demonstrates interference.
  • Path Difference: Δx = d sin θ ≈ dy/D
  • Bright Fringes (Maxima): Δx = nλ (for n = 0, 1, 2...)
  • Dark Fringes (Minima): Δx = (n + 0.5)λ
  • Fringe Width (β): β = λD/d

Diffraction

The bending of light waves around the corners of an obstacle or through an aperture.

  • Single Slit Diffraction: Central bright maximum flanked by secondary maxima and minima.
  • Minima Condition: a sin θ = nλ (where a is slit width).

Polarization

Restricting light vibrations to a single plane, proving light is a transverse wave.

  • Brewster’s Law: μ = tan ip
  • Malus’s Law: I = I0 cos² θ

notes.title: Current Electricity — Detailed Notes
notes.content:
Kirchhoff’s Laws

  • First Law (KCL): ΣI = 0 (Conservation of Charge). Sum of currents entering a junction equals sum leaving.
  • Second Law (KVL): ΣΔV = 0 (Conservation of Energy). Algebraic sum of potential changes in a closed loop is zero.

Potentiometer

A device to measure EMF and internal resistance without drawing current.

  • Comparing EMFs: E1/E2 = l1/l2
  • Internal Resistance (r): r = R((l1/l2) - 1)

notes.title: Modern Physics — Detailed Notes
notes.content:

  • Quantized Angular Momentum: L = nh/2π
  • Energy Levels: En = -13.6/n² eV (for Hydrogen)

notes.title: Atomic Structure — Detailed Notes

Quantum Numbers

  • Azimuthal (l): Subshell shape (0 to n-1)

Mixing of atomic orbitals to form new hybrid orbitals equivalent in energy.

  • Ribosomes: Protein synthesis factories (70S in prokaryotes, 80S in eukaryotes).
  • Golgi Body: Packaging and secretion.

Cell Division

  • Mitosis: Equational division (2n → 2n). Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase.
  • Meiosis: Reductional division (2n → n). Homologous pairing and crossing over in Prophase I.

Breakdown of food. Enzymes: Pepsin (Stomach), Trypsin/Lipase (Pancreas). Absorption occurs in villi.

Double circulation. Cardiac cycle (0.8s). SA Node is the pacemaker.

Excretion

Nephron structure. Urine formation: Ultrafiltration, Reabsorption, Secretion.

  • Translation: mRNA to Protein. Occurs in ribosomes. tRNA carries amino acids.

notes.title: वीर पुर्खा (कविता) - सारांश
notes.content:
मूल भाव

यस कवितामा कविले नेपाली वीर पुर्खाहरूको वीरता, साहस र बलिदानको गाथा गाएका छन्। नेपालको सिमाना पूर्वमा टिस्टा र पश्चिममा काँगडासम्म पुर्याउने पुर्खाहरूको योगदानलाई सम्मान गरिएको छ।

मुख्य बुँदाहरू

  • नेपालीहरूको वीरता र स्वाभिमान।
  • प्राकृतिक कठिनाइहरू (पहाड, नदी) छिचोल्दै अघि बढ्ने साहस।
  • इतिहासको गौरवमय क्षणहरूको स्मरण।

notes.title: गाउँको माया (कथा) - समीक्षा
notes.content:
कथाको सार

यो एक सामाजिक कथा हो जसले वैदेशिक रोजगारी र शहर पस्ने प्रवृत्तिका कारण गाउँहरू रित्तिँदै गएको यथार्थ चित्रण गर्छ। गाउँको अर्गानिक जीवनशैली, आत्मीयता र प्रकृतिप्रेमलाई मुख्य विषय बनाइएको छ।

सन्देश

गाउँको विकास र संरक्षण गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता। आफ्नो माटो र संस्कृतिप्रतिको प्रेम।

notes.title: Story: Neighbours (Tim Winton)
notes.content:

A young couple moves into a multicultural suburb. Initially prejudiced against their European neighbors, they gradually learn to appreciate the community's warmth and support, especially after the birth of their child.

Themes

Multiculturalism, transition, prejudice vs. acceptance, and community bonding.

notes.title: आमाको सपना (कविता) - विश्लेषण
notes.content:
कवि: गोपालप्रसाद रिमाल

यस कवितामा आमा (नेपाल आमा) ले आफ्नो छोरा (नेपाली जनता) सँग क्रान्ति र परिवर्तनको सपना देखेको कुरा व्यक्त गरिएको छ। अन्धकार हटेर सुनौलो बिहानी आउने विश्वास प्रकट गरिएको छ।

  • आमा: नेपाल राष्ट्र।
  • छोरा: परिवर्तनकारी युवा/जनता।

notes.title: Calculus: Limits & Derivatives
notes.content:
Limits

lim(x→a) (xⁿ - aⁿ)/(x - a) = n·aⁿ⁻¹

lim(x→0) (sin x)/x = 1

lim(x→0) (eˣ - 1)/x = 1

Derivatives

  • d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹
  • d/dx(sin x) = cos x
  • d/dx(ln x) = 1/x
  • Product Rule: d/dx(uv) = u'v + uv'

notes.title: Integrals: Standard Forms
notes.content:
Indefinite Integrals

  • ∫ xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C
  • ∫ (1/x) dx = ln|x| + C
  • ∫ eˣ dx = eˣ + C

Integration by Parts

∫ u v dx = u ∫v dx - ∫(u' ∫v dx) dx

Order of choice (ILATE): Inverse, Log, Alg, Trig, Exp.

notes.title: Genetics: Molecular Basis
notes.content:
DNA Structure

Double helix model (Watson & Crick). Nucleotides: Sugar + Phosphate + Nitrogen Base (A, T, G, C).

Base Pairing: A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds).

Central Dogma

DNA → (Transcription) → mRNA → (Translation) → Protein.

Mendel's Laws

1. Law of Dominance.

2. Law of Segregation (Purity of Gametes).

3. Law of Independent Assortment.

notes.title: Electrostatics — Gauss Law & Potential
notes.content:
Gauss's Law

Total flux Φ through a closed surface is q/ε₀. Φ = ∮ E·dA = q/ε₀.

Applications

  • Line Charge: E = λ / (2πε₀r)
  • Sheet Charge: E = σ / (2ε₀)
  • Spherical Shell: E = 0 (inside), E = kQ/r² (outside)

Electric Potential

Work done to move unit positive charge. V = kQ/r. Equipotential surfaces are perpendicular to E-field lines.

notes.title: Waves & Sound — Doppler Effect
notes.content:
Doppler Effect

Apparent change in frequency due to relative motion.

f' = f (v ± v₀) / (v ∓ vₛ)

  • Observer towards source: (+) numerator.
  • Source towards observer: (-) denominator.

Stationary Waves

Formed by superposition of two identical waves traveling in opposite directions. Nodes (zero amplitude), Antinodes (max amplitude).

Open Pipe: f = nv/2L (All harmonics). Closed Pipe: f = nv/4L (Odd harmonics only).

notes.title: Current Electricity — Circuits
notes.content:
Kirchhoff's Laws

  • KCL (Junction Rule): ΣI = 0 (Conservation of Charge).
  • KVL (Loop Rule): ΣΔV = 0 (Conservation of Energy).

Potentiometer

Measures EMF accurately (no current drawn). Principle: V ∝ l.

Comparison of EMFs: E₁/E₂ = l₁/l₂. Internal Resistance: r = R(l₁/l₂ - 1).

Wheatstone Bridge

Balanced condition: P/Q = R/S. No current flows through galvanometer.

notes.title: Magnetic Effects — Biot-Savart & Ampere
notes.content:
Biot-Savart Law

dB = (μ₀/4π) (I dl sinθ / r²).

Straight Wire: B = μ₀I / 2πr (Infinite length).

Circular Loop (Center): B = μ₀I / 2R.

Ampere's Circuital Law

∮ B·dl = μ₀ I_enclosed. Used for Solenoid (B = μ₀nI) and Toroid.

Force on Conductor

F = I(L × B) = BIL sinθ. Force between parallel wires: F/L = μ₀I₁I₂ / 2πd.

notes.title: Alternating Current (AC)
notes.content:
LCR Series Circuit

Impedance Z = √[R² + (X_L - X_C)²]. Phase φ = tan⁻¹((X_L - X_C)/R).

Resonance: X_L = X_C ⇒ f = 1 / (2π√LC). Z is minimum (R), Current is maximum.

Power: P = V_rms I_rms cosφ (cosφ = Power Factor = R/Z).

notes.title: States of Matter — Real Gases
notes.content:
Ideal vs Real Gases

Ideal gases follow PV=nRT at all conditions. Real gases deviate at high P and low T.

Van der Waals Equation

(P + an²/V²)(V - nb) = nRT

  • a: Intermolecular attraction correction.
  • b: Volume correction (excluded volume).

Dalton's Law

Total Pressure P_total = P₁ + P₂ + ... + Pₙ (Partial pressures).

notes.title: Ionic Equilibrium — pH & Buffers
notes.content:
Ostwald's Dilution Law

Degree of dissociation α = √(Ka/C) for weak electrolytes.

pH Concept

pH = -log[H⁺]. pH + pOH = 14.

Buffer Solutions

Resist pH change. Henderson-Hasselbalch Eq:

Acidic Buffer: pH = pKa + log([Salt]/[Acid]).

Basic Buffer: pOH = pKb + log([Salt]/[Base]).

notes.title: Heavy Metals — Extraction
notes.content:
Iron (Fe) — Hematite

Blast Furnace: Reduction by CO.

  • Zone of Reduction: Fe₂O₃ + CO → Fe.
  • Zone of Fusion: Limestone (Flux) + Silica (Impurity) → Slag (CaSiO₃).

Copper (Cu) — Copper Pyrites

Process: Froth Flotation → Roasting → Smelting (Matte: Cu₂S + FeS) → Bessemerization (Blister Copper) → Refining.

Zinc (Zn) — Zinc Blende

Roasting (ZnO) → Carbon Reduction (Vertical Retort Process).

notes.title: Transition Metals (d-block)
notes.content:
General Properties

  • Variable Oxidation States: ns and (n-1)d electrons participate.
  • Color: d-d transition of unpaired electrons.
  • Magnetic Properties: Paramagnetic due to unpaired electrons. Magnetic Moment μ = √[n(n+2)] BM.
  • Complex Formation: Small size, high charge, vacant d-orbitals.

Lanthanide Contraction

Poor shielding by 4f electrons causes atomic size to decrease steadily, making Zr/Hf similar.

notes.title: Botany — Angiosperm Families
notes.content:
Cruciferae (Brassicaceae)

Mustard Family. Flower: Tetramerous, Cruciform corolla. Stamens: Tetradynamous (2+4). Fruit: Siliqua.

Floral Formula: ⊕ ⚥ K2+2 C4 A2+4 G(2).

Solanaceae

Potato Family. Flower: Pentamerous. Anthers: Epipetalous. Ovary: Obliquely placed, swollen placenta.

Floral Formula: ⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2).

Leguminosae (Papilionaceae)

Pea Family. Corolla: Papilionaceous (Vexillary aestivation - Standard, Wings, Keel). Stamens: Diadelphous (9)+1.

Floral Formula: % ⚥ K(5) C1+2+(2) A(9)+1 G1.

notes.title: Nervous System — Synapse & Reflex
notes.content:
Synaptic Transmission

Electrical signal → Ca²⁺ influx → Neurotransmitter release (Acetylcholine) → Binds to receptors → Na⁺ influx → Depolarization.

Reflex Arc

Receptor → Sensory Neuron → CNS (Interneuron) → Motor Neuron → Effector (Muscle). Involuntary and rapid.

notes.title: Endocrine System — Hormones
notes.content:
Pituitary Gland (Master Gland)

  • Anterior: GH (Growth), TSH, ACTH, FSH/LH (Gonads), Prolactin.
  • Posterior: ADH (Water balance), Oxytocin (Birth/Milk).

Other Glands

  • Thyroid: Thyroxine (T3/T4) - Metabolism.
  • Pancreas: Insulin (Beta cells - lowers glucose), Glucagon (Alpha cells - raises glucose).
  • Adrenal: Adrenaline (Flight/Fight), Cortisol (Stress).

notes.title: Applied Biology — Biotech
notes.content:
Tissue Culture

Growing cells in sterile medium (nutrient agar). Totipotency: Ability of a cell to generate whole plant.

Steps: Explant → Callus → Organogenesis → Plantlet → Hardening.

Recombinant DNA Technology

1. Isolation of DNA. 2. Cutting with Restriction Endonucleases (Molecular Scissors). 3. Ligation (DNA Ligase) into Vector (Plasmid). 4. Transformation into Host (E. coli). 5. Selection & Culture.

notes.title: Number Systems & Boolean Algebra
notes.content:
Conversions

  • Binary to Decimal: Sum of digit × 2ⁿ.
  • Decimal to Binary: Repeated division by 2.
  • Hexadecimal: Base 16 (0-9, A-F). 1 Hex digit = 4 Binary bits.

Logic Gates

  • Universal Gates: NAND, NOR (Can implement any Boolean function).
  • XOR: Output 1 if inputs are different.

Boolean Laws

De Morgan's: (A+B)' = A'.B' and (A.B)' = A' + B'.

notes.title: Networking — OSI Model
notes.content:
OSI Reference Model (7 Layers)

  1. Physical: Bits, Cables, Hubs.
  2. Data Link: Frames, MAC Address, Switch.
  3. Network: Packets, IP Address, Router.
  4. Transport: Segments, TCP/UDP (Reliability).
  5. Session: Session management.
  6. Presentation: Encryption, Compression.
  7. Application: HTTP, FTP, SMTP (User Interface).

Topologies

Star (Central hub), Bus (Single cable), Ring, Mesh (Full connection).

notes.title: C Programming — Struct vs Union
notes.content:
Structure (struct)

Allocates memory for ALL members. Size = Sum of members (plus padding).

struct Point { int x; int y; };

Union

Allocates memory for LARGEST member only. Shared memory space.

Useful for memory saving when only one member is used at a time.
